body: The spec is admirably concrete, but two claims don't hold up on inspection. First, the sourcing of mixing enthalpy: FR-003 insists the binary interaction parameters come from 'NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables (2022 edition)'. JANAF is a thermochemical database for compounds and pure species; it does not tabulate the equiatomic binary mixing enthalpies Ω_ij used in the Takeuchi–Inoue/Miedema formalism that this descriptor actually requires. The stated independence rationale ('distinct from the experimental yield strength source') is sound, but the named source appears to be the wrong one — the field-standard source is the Miedema-model tabulation of DFT/calculated binary enthalpies. As written, the requirement may be unimplementable as specified. Second, there is a real tension between FR-004 and FR-005: FR-004 mandates an 80/20 train-test split, while FR-005 reports metrics from Repeated 5-Fold CV 'on the holdout set' — cross-validation and holdout evaluation are conflated, and US-3's test (matching R² to 1e-5 with a fixed seed) cannot be specified until this is disambiguated. Third, a smaller logical wrinkle: FR-004 requires duplicate compositions to be assigned to the same partition to avoid leakage, but FR-007 aggregates duplicates before modeling, so no duplicates should remain to assign — one of the two requirements is redundant or the ordering is unstated. Finally, the assumption that pooled yield strengths are 'measured under comparable conditions' quietly carries most of the scientific risk: yield strength in BCC alloys is notoriously sensitive to grain size, heat treatment, and test temperature, and composition-only features may simply proxy processing history. The null-result framing in the project description anticipates this, but the spec's success criteria (SC-001) don't require any processing-condition covariate or even a sensitivity check, so a modest R² could be silently confounded rather than informative about composition per se.
